local_checks.invariant: After `sessions-revoke`, no timer/queued write of the running app may bring revoked sessions or app passwords back; the reload marker is the only protection and it is checked only at request start
local_checks.result: Two processes on one scratch DATA_DIR (app in-process, CLI via Bun.spawn). Scenario A: dav PROPFIND with app password (queues 5 s updateSoon timer), CLI sessions-revoke alice (disk: 0 alice app passwords), wait 6.5 s with no request: app-passwords.json again holds the revoked item (1) and the next PROPFIND with the old secret returns 207 (not 401); it stays on disk. Scenario B control (next request before the timer): PROPFIND 401, disk 0 after the timer window. Scenario C: session of carol, CLI revoke (sessions.json 0 carol entries), purgeExpiredSessions() (the hourly housekeeping function) writes memory back: sessions.json has the carol session again and GET /api/session returns carol. Not run: a request landing between CLI write and marker touch (source: the CLI does flushAll then writes the marker, a request in that gap sees old marker and keeps memory; the following request reloads from disk, so the gap alone is self-healing unless a timer write lands there too); persist retry path (same cause, not run).

confirmed (medium): Reproduced twice in the sandbox: app-passwords.json 0 items after the CLI, 1 after the timer, PROPFIND 207 with the revoked secret. Control (request right after the CLI): 401, disk 0. Session variant: after purgeExpiredSessions() GET /api/session returns carol.

parent_note: the CLI process and the running app write the same JSON files; a timer write of the app (app-password lastUsedAt after 5 s, hourly session purge, getSession save, queued persist retries) landing between the CLI write and the next request could bring revoked sessions or app passwords back. Prior finding cli-revoke-not-applied-to-webdav was re-checked from source only. Local check: two bun processes on one scratch DATA_DIR, an active WebDAV client, sessions-revoke, authenticate again after the timer.
parent_hardening: reloadIfChangedByCli compares mtimeMs of cli-changed; two CLI runs within the same filesystem timestamp granularity could be missed (not exercised)
cli.ts reset-2fa/sessions-revoke load their own copy of users.json at start; concurrent app writes to users.json between that load and the CLI save would be lost (no locking between processes)

local_checks.invariant: event-loop cost of the subtree walk and deflate of an anonymous GET /api/batch/:token is bounded or yields
local_checks.result: Anonymous visitor on public space with default guest permissions. Tree of N one-byte files in nested folders, one batch of the top folder. A probe process (separate process, real loopback server) polling /api/session every 50 ms: N=2000 max probe latency 342 and 491 ms (zip total 348/501 ms); N=20000 max probe latency 3755 and 3691 ms (zip total 3772/3718 ms). Timers in-process: 0 interval ticks fired during the whole zip. Direct collectZipItems alone: 6-8 ms (2000), 45-58 ms (20000), so the synchronous walk is minor; the stall is the microtask-only zipStream pipeline (about 0.17 ms per entry) that never yields to the event loop. Linear in entry count, no entry/depth cap. Share-folder download uses the same zipStream, not run separately for this check.

local_checks.invariant: a zip download whose body is never read cannot hold codec slots that starve other zips (user download, backup)
local_checks.result: Real Bun server on loopback, 4 anonymous visitors (each own session, own batch token) GET /api/batch/:token with three 6 MB random base64 files and read only the headers: a 5th visitor zip of a 23-byte file and a zipStream call standing in for the backup both TIMEOUT at 12 s (4 of 4 runs; with 1.5 MB files 3 of 5 runs, because socket buffers can absorb a small zip). Same with 4 holders on a folder share link: TIMEOUT at 12 s in 2 of 2 runs. Baseline victim 5-130 ms.

local_checks.invariant: aborting the client request releases the codec slot
local_checks.result: After AbortController.abort() on the 4 held connections, with 1.5 s wait, the victim zip finished in 4-11 ms and the backup-like zip in 1-2 ms in every run (batch 9 runs, share 2 runs). Cancellation releases the slots; the slot is held only while the client keeps the connection open without reading.
confirmed (medium): totalMs 3359 and 3269, timer ticks 0, max loop gap equal to the whole download, in two sandboxed runs.

unresolved: validation_budget_exhausted: zipstream-unread-body-holds-codec-slots has no independent Phase 3 verifier (5th candidate in fingerprint order; 4 Phase 3 slots in the 12-agent budget); hunter-only evidence, not a finding

validation_budget_exhausted: zipstream-no-yield-eventloop-stall-large-tree was confirmed by Phase 3 verifier v04 but has no Phase 5 record verifier (3 Phase 5 slots used in fingerprint order); not in findings.json
parent_note: archive creation has no unit. GET /api/batch/:token (anonymous by default) and a folder share download walk the whole subtree synchronously (collectZipItems, no entry or depth cap) and deflate on the main thread with no concurrency cap. Local check: event-loop delay of the walk on a bounded tree and of N concurrent anonymous batch downloads; does the generator stop when the client disconnects.
parent_hardening: The synchronous readdir walk alone is cheap (about 50 ms for 20,000 entries); the cost is the zipStream pipeline, not collectZipItems.
BATCH_PER_CALLER and BATCH_MAX cap only unused tokens; a token can be fetched repeatedly until it expires (5 min) so the cap does not limit concurrent downloads.

local_checks.invariant: An anonymous public-space search must not scan rows outside the caller's folder or block the shared event loop for more than a bounded, small time
local_checks.result: Query is bounded to root plus a rel range (e.rel >= start/ and < start0) of the caller's start folder, so a public-space query reads only rows under /public, not other homes. instr runs synchronously on bun:sqlite, limit is capped at 500, FTS_CAP 1000 caps FTS candidates, walk fallback is capped at 50,000 entries and awaits between batches. No rate limit or cache on GET /api/search (need read only). shares.ts has no search path.

local_checks.invariant: Measured cost of slow-path anonymous searches (1-2 char miss, 1000+ hit needle, filters, walk fallback) at 50k and 200k entries
local_checks.result: Sandboxed in-process run, anonymous session, space=public, guest read. 50k entries (10k public): 2-char miss 4-16 ms, 1-char 5 ms, common needle 7-9 ms, filter+sort 5 ms. 200k entries (100k public, 100k in 5 homes): 2-char miss 35-49 ms, 1-char 34-45 ms, common needle 40-47 ms, size-desc sort 44-45 ms, filter 33-35 ms, 3-char FTS miss 1 ms; each run twice. Cost tracks the public subtree size (about 0.4 ms per 1k rows), not the whole storage; the synchronous query blocks the loop for about its duration (my lag probe did not capture it since the timer fires after the sync call, so duration equals stall). Walk fallback (index off) 24-62 ms at 50k and about 140 ms at 200k, truncated at 50k seen, event loop yielding (lag 1-14 ms). Index build 2.1 s (50k) and 9.4 s (200k), yielding between batches. No shared-impact threshold reached at these sizes.

parent_note: search was reviewed for access control only. For a needle under 3 characters or with more than 1000 trigram hits the query runs synchronously on bun:sqlite as an instr() scan over every indexed entry of the storage root, callable by anonymous visitors on the public space with no rate limit. Local check: time a 2-character non-matching anonymous query on a seeded index of bounded size and the event-loop delay.
parent_hardening: GET /api/search has no per-IP rate limit or result cache; each anonymous 1-2 char query runs a synchronous instr() scan over the public subtree (about 35-49 ms at 100k public rows, roughly linear, so a public folder of 1M+ entries would stall the loop about 0.4 s per request). Consider moving it to a worker, requiring needle length 3 for visitors, or a per-IP limiter.
FTS path for needles of 3+ chars with more than FTS_CAP hits falls back to the instr scan in name order with LIMIT; a rare-miss ordering by mtime or size cannot stop early, same linear subtree cost.
Search stalls only scale with the size of the public folder for visitors; extreme sizes (millions of rows) were not measured, to stay within the no-stress rule.

local_checks.invariant: A WebDAV PUT whose app password is revoked, whose account is deleted/re-created, or whose rights are lowered while the body streams must not complete as the old principal
local_checks.result: In-process app, ReadableStream body fed in two pieces, 2 rounds x (known length, no length). (a) delete + recreate same name (other home, and same home with read-only perms): PUT 201, file written to the path resolved at start; new account is charged (usage 10 B in its counter for a file outside its home, cache entry added through the name-keyed commit). (b) app password revoked mid-body: a new PROPFIND with it gives 401 but the running PUT gives 201 and the file lands. (c) permissions changed to read-only: PUT 201 (Space.perms is a copy taken at start); quota lowered to 3 B: PUT 507 (the user object is live, so quota is re-read at holdNow).

local_checks.invariant: PUT /api/content after a slow antivirus scan must not write as an account that was deleted, re-created or downgraded; office saveVersion re-checks
local_checks.result: Fake clamd delaying 1.5 s. Delete + recreate (other home and same home, read-only perms): PUT /api/content 200, new content written to the old resolved path, 23 B charged to the re-created account counter. Permissions changed to read-only during the scan (no quota change): 200 and file written. Quota lowered to 3 B: 507. Source: src/office.ts saveVersion calls tokenFile(t,['write']) again after the download and scan (line 375), so it does not have the gap; ownerOfPath(abs) in files.ts is taken before the scan (stale owner for versions).
confirmed (low): PROPFIND after revoke 401; PUT 201; file f.txt contains helloworld (two runs).

parent_note: parallel write paths to the confirmed uploads/inflight-complete-survives-account-drop: a slow WebDAV PUT (and PUT /api/content, the office save) fixes the quota user and target before the body and the scan, and re-checks neither the account instance nor the app password afterwards; dropUploadsOf cannot see them. Local check: slow DAV PUT, delete and re-create the user or revoke the app password, finish the body, see where the file lands and who is charged.
parent_hardening: src/office.ts saveVersion re-runs tokenFile(t,['write']) after the download and gate (line 375), so the office save does not share the gap; ownerOfPath(abs) at line 372 is taken after the scan too.
src/quota.ts keys reserved/cache by lowercase username only, so a re-created account of the same name inherits holds and commits of the old account until the 60 s recount.
